excerpt: Use a Sharjah waterfront investment checklist to verify the unit, ownership right, building maintenance, costs, rental evidence and exit.
introduction:
A Sharjah waterfront apartment investment needs the same financial and legal checks as any property, plus a close look at the actual view, access and building maintenance. Assess the home’s condition, likely rent, running costs and resale market alongside its coastal setting.

Use this checklist for the exact unit and engage qualified advisers when a technical or legal issue is beyond your expertise. The financial example demonstrates how to compare the full cost and annual income of a home.
takeaways: Verify the actual view, access, building condition and maintenance arrangements for the unit.
Confirm the buyer's ownership right, registered project, transfer obligations and current charges.
Calculate net income after vacancy and owner costs, and test repairs and resale risk.

sections.heading: 1. Verify the actual setting
sections.body:
Ask for the unit number, floor plan, orientation and parking, then visit the apartment if ready. Check the view from the rooms and balcony, the route to the waterfront and whether access is public, shared or subject to building rules. Inspect the outlook from the specific apartment and its outdoor areas.

[Shurooq's Maryam Island overview](https://shurooq.gov.ae/portfolio/maryam-island) and [Bayut's Al Khan guide](https://www.bayut.com/area-guides/al-khan-sharjah/) provide examples of Sharjah waterfront settings. The [Maryam Island pros and cons guide](/journal/maryam-island-apartment-buying-pros-and-cons) discusses unit-level checks. These sources do not confirm the condition or availability of your apartment.

Review nearby construction and the current and planned uses around the building. Ask what is contractual and what remains a proposal.

table.caption: Waterfront investment checks
rows: Actual unit visit, plan and current access rules
Inspection, maintenance history and specialist report if needed
Authority confirmation, title and seller's right to transfer
Charge statement, quotes and comparable signed leases
Comparable completed sales, selling costs and loan balance

sections.heading: 2. Inspect the unit and maintenance
sections.body:
Check windows, seals, balconies, cooling, plumbing and visible moisture. Ask about the condition and maintenance of exposed fittings and common areas. Coastal exposure can affect maintenance needs, but it should be assessed for the individual building rather than assumed to have caused damage.

Request the service-charge statement, maintenance history, management contact and information about any known major work. Ask which insurance is held for shared areas and what cover the owner needs for the apartment. Obtain a qualified inspection if there are concerns about water ingress, corrosion or another technical issue.

For an off-plan unit, review the signed specification, completion and handover provisions. Check the project's current status and payment process with the relevant authority and developer.

sections.heading: 3. Verify ownership and transaction costs
sections.body:
Ask Sharjah's registration department to confirm the buyer's right for the exact property. Review title or initial registration, seller authority, any mortgage or tenancy and required clearance. The [Sharjah eligibility guide](/journal/how-to-check-foreign-ownership-eligibility-in-sharjah) explains the evidence to request.

Obtain an itemised current quote for registration, brokerage, finance and other charges. Add initial work and furnishing to the price, and keep a separate reserve. Do not assume a fee or ownership right applies to every waterfront project.

Verify payment instructions independently and keep receipts and the official registration outcome. Seek qualified advice if the documents or contractual obligations are unclear.

sections.heading: 4. Calculate income after costs
sections.body:
Suppose a sample apartment requires AED 1,200,000 in total acquisition cost. Assume AED 80,000 annual rent, AED 8,000 vacancy allowance and AED 18,000 of owner costs. Net operating income is AED 54,000, or 4.5% of the total cost, before finance, tax and sale costs. These example figures show how rent and annual costs combine in a yield calculation.

The chart shows the rent, deductions and resulting income as parts of one calculation. Use recent signed leases for similar units, including size, condition, parking, view and furnishing. Compare asking rents with signed leases and the income collected from similar homes.

Test a longer vacancy and higher repair or service charge. A view may help tenant appeal, but its effect on rent must be supported by comparable evidence.

chart.title: Example waterfront rental calculation
chart.note: Sample figures; net income equals rent less deductions and excludes finance, tax and sale costs.

sections.heading: 5. Check insurance, access and intended use
sections.body:
Ask the insurer what risks and parts of the property are covered, what exclusions apply and how claims are handled. Review the building's rules for balconies, pets, alterations and access to shared facilities. A sea view does not necessarily mean private beach access or an included berth.

If you intend short-term accommodation, confirm the current licensing and building requirements with the relevant Sharjah authorities before assuming that use is permitted. A long-term residential lease has different obligations.

Visit the building at the times a tenant might use it and test parking and travel to work or services. A convenient promenade does not automatically make every daily journey convenient.

sections.heading: 6. Assess the exit and downside
sections.body:
Look for recent completed sales of similar units and separate them from asking prices. Record the floor, view, size, condition and tenancy so differences are visible. Include selling expenses and any outstanding loan in an eventual proceeds estimate.

Test a lower sale price, longer vacancy and an unexpected repair. Keep a cash reserve and do not rely on a forecast of appreciation to meet a contractual payment. If the comparable evidence is thin, use a range and seek a suitable professional valuation.

Keep the evidence dated and update it if the market, building condition or financing changes. A past sale can inform a range, but it does not ensure that a new buyer will pay the same amount or that a sale will complete within a particular period.

sections.heading: Request current waterfront options
sections.body:
Browse [Aliyas Maryam Island projects](/projects?emirate=Sharjah&area=sharjah-maryam-island) and [Al Khan projects](/projects?emirate=Sharjah&area=sharjah-al-khan). [Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget, nationality and intended use.

Ask which units are currently available and request the exact plan, ownership documents and current charges. Compare the evidence for each specific home. Verify the property and official requirements before committing.
